questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The menopause and why it should be discussed openly
How doctors treat hot flushes and night sweats at home
Why women in Britain are having children later in life
Michelle Obama's life and career after leaving the White House
questions.why: They discuss the menopause and women trying to make it more visible in society.

questions.q: According to Georgina, how can going through the menopause feel?
options: Exciting, because life becomes easier
The same for every woman
Lonely, both at home and at work
Painful only for a few days
questions.why: She says living through it can be isolating, both personally and professionally.

questions.q: Why does Georgina mention Michelle Obama?
options: She is a doctor who studies the menopause
She is a famous woman who has started talking about it
She writes a newsletter about healthy ageing
She thinks the subject should stay private
questions.why: Georgina says high-profile women like Michelle Obama have started speaking up.

questions.q: Why, according to Dr Nighat Arif, is there silence around the menopause?
options: Because doctors don't really understand what causes it
Because it only affects a small number of women
Because it is a new medical condition
Because it is about getting older
questions.why: She says menopause is about getting old, something no one wants to be reminded of.

questions.q: What point does Dr Arif make about older women today?
options: Most of them stop working after having their children
They are less productive than younger women
Many work hard, care for others and earn money
They should rely more on their grown-up children
questions.why: She says women are becoming more productive at work, are caregivers and sometimes the financial providers.

options: An American writer with a newsletter on healthy ageing
A British doctor specialising in women's health
A BBC presenter of The Conversation
A scientist who studies hormones
questions.why: She is an American writer who publishes 'The Menopause Cheat Sheet' about healthy ageing.

questions.q: According to Barbara Hannah Grufferman, what is one of the biggest problems for women over 45?
options: Finding a doctor who understands the menopause
Paying for medicine
Getting enough sleep at night
Unfair treatment because of their age
questions.why: She says 'one of the biggest complications, I think, is ageism'.

questions.q: What does she mean by a 'double whammy' for women going through the menopause?
options: They have to work full-time and look after young children
They face age discrimination and physical symptoms at once
They suffer from hot flushes and night sweats at the same time
They lose their job and their pension in the same year
questions.why: She says ageism plus physical symptoms that affect work and home together make a double whammy.
